---
title: How the ratings work
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/site.R")
publication <- read_publication("out/release/elo")
spec <- publication$manifest$analysis$specification
```

## The published model

Elo updates a team's rating after a completed match, using the result and the
opponent's rating. Test, ODI, and T20I matches form separate rating pools.

```{r}
#| results: asis
settings <- data.frame(
  Setting = c("Initial rating", "Expected score", "Ties", "No-result matches", "Update order"),
  Value = c(spec$initial_rating, spec$expectation, spec$ties, spec$no_result, spec$order)
)
knitr::kable(settings, format = "html", escape = TRUE)
```

Draws and ties count as half-results. A regulation tie resolved by a tiebreaker
is treated as a tie when the source records it that way. Abandoned, cancelled,
and no-result matches do not update either team's rating.

The implementation is `r spec$implementation`, version `r spec$version`, from
the R package [EloRating](https://cran.r-project.org/package=EloRating).
The complete specification is included in the [publication metadata](../out/release/elo/manifest.json).

## Selecting K

K controls how strongly each result changes a rating. Each format selects its
own value using a January 1 cutoff in the publication year and the preceding
five complete calendar years. Each candidate's forecasts use only results completed
before the match starts. The selected value minimizes average squared error of
the expected score, including draws and ties as 0.5. This is a grid optimum for
that scoring rule and period, not a universally optimal constant.

```{r}
#| results: asis
selection <- readr::read_csv("out/release/elo/k_selection.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
knitr::kable(selection[c("format", "k", "origin", "tuning_start", "tuning_end", "n_tuning")],
  format = "html", escape = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)
```

Selection is recomputed from the saved source version, so corrections to prior
years can change K within the publication year. The current partial year cannot
select K. Ratings do incorporate completed
matches from that year after selection. Search candidates are integers 1–200
and 220–400 in increments of 20; exact loss ties prefer the smaller K.
At least 100 tuning matches and observations in each tuning year are required.

Download the [selection results](../out/release/elo/k_selection.csv) and
[candidate loss curves](../out/release/elo/k_tuning.csv). Historical evaluation
also compares three- and ten-year windows with the fixed K=100 baseline.
Those comparisons are retrospective; they are not blinded confirmation.
The same selection rule is used for each format, including T20Is where the
historical improvement over K=100 was small.

## Dates and history

Matches enter on their completion date. Same-day results use the deterministic
ordering shown above. Monthly downloads contain calendar-month-end snapshots;
the charts show end-of-day match updates, including the latest partial month.
Ratings carry forward between results. The charts do not smooth the estimates.

Histories are reconstructed from the current saved source version. They do not
prove what could have been known from the source at an earlier date. Git history
records successive actual publications.
Each publication replays the entire format's history with its selected K.
Consequently, the historical curves are retrospective estimates using a current
parameter; they are not the forecasts used to evaluate annual selection.

## Which teams are ranked?

Teams are active if they have played a rated match within `r spec$active_days`
days. Teams with fewer than `r spec$provisional_matches` rated matches are
provisional. Equal ratings share a competition rank. Inactive teams remain in the
CSV without a current rank. These are our display rules, independent of ICC rules.

## What the ratings leave out

This baseline has no venue or margin adjustment, inactivity decay, player-lineup
effects, or uncertainty intervals. A fixed K controls responsiveness to results;
the trajectory is an estimate under those choices, not directly observed ability.
Sparse schedules and weak connections between opponent groups can limit comparisons.

We plan to compare richer models using chronological forecast evaluation. The
[research agenda](research.qmd) describes these choices, including the distinction
between live predictions and retrospective historical estimates.

## Correctness and reproducibility

Source responses are saved and checked before modeling. Published files are
verified against their recorded hashes before the website renders. The site
reads saved results and does not refit the model.

The [correctness audit](correctness.qmd) documents the old outcome and timing
errors, the corrections, and the numerical validation. Code and tests are
available in the [repository](https://github.com/outside-edge/side_order).
